text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak said he was worried violence would escalate because of Israel building settlements and violating the rights of Arabs and Moslems in East Jerusalem. In a televised address he said the peace process faced a grave test. In a meeting with army officers in Suez he said that Egypt's aim was that Sudan should recover its health and shake off terrorist gangs.
- Mubarak received a letter from Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh on the peace process.
- Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni arrives in Egypt today at the start of a two-day visit. He will meet Mubarak.
- Egyptian opposition parties said they completely reject the policy of fait accompli Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is trying to impose on Arabs and Palestinians.

- U.S. ambassador Edward Walker said his country would resume contacts with Israel in the framework of its steps in the Middle East peace process. He said he expected a U.S. demarche to reach a formula to save the peace process.
- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi said the security forces would go ahead with total confrontation with fugitive terrorist groups after cutting off the supplies and money which used to reach them.
- The trial of Israel's spies was postponed until May 18.
- Egypt's ambassador to Singapore said the volume of trade between the two countries would reach $500 million and that businessmen in Singapore were investing more in Egypt.
- Mubarak said the only solution was for Israel to stop building in East Jerusalem.
- Health Minister Ismail Sallam won 20,000 pounds ($5,900) damages in a libel case against the newspaper al-Naba al-Watani.
- Central Bank governor Ismail Hassan said the Egyptian economy was performing well and was constantly progressing.
- Banks will take next Sunday and Monday off for Coptic Easter and the spring festival Shamm el-Nassim, as well as May 1 for Labour Day and May 8 for Islamic New Year.
